proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) originally asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and 'fix whatever is causing wrong bills' (CL-01). Dispute volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline to 1180 in August and 1260 in September (E-05); slow ticket response (E-03) and a tariff change (E-02, E-07) were ruled out. An initial theory tying this to a field route-completion/staffing shortfall (E-04, E-06) was invalidated by E-12, which traced the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41%) instead to AMI billing-import rejections. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) established these 1240 bills are fully explained: AMI firmware v4.2 records in 0.1 m3 vs legacy m3 (E-13), and billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (coincident with the surge), compares raw register values with no unit scaling (E-14), producing 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION + 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED = 1240 (E-12, confirmed by E-15, E-16, E-17). No automated bill writes occurred; querying stayed read-only per K-BILLWRITE. The remaining 1785 disputed bills (59%, ACTUAL read type, E-01) are NOT yet explained - the critical obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE remains OPEN. A work item claiming to resolve it was marked DONE but cites only the already-known ESTIMATED-pool evidence (E-17), flagging an inconsistency between the plan's status and the obligation it was meant to close. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS): the confirmed ESTIMATED-pool finding is delivered, while the unresolved ACTUAL-read majority cause, the undeployable structural fix, and other open items are carried forward explicitly as known limitations rather than blocking release.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an auto-answering AI agent that also fixes the billing cause; treated as a claim to test, not an instruction to execute.
Dispute surge confirmed: ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline rose to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-05); slow response (E-03) and tariff change (E-02, E-07) ruled out as causes.

A first explanation (route-completion shortfall 88% vs 95% target, E-04, attributed by SH-FIELD to staffing shortage, E-06) was invalidated once E-12 showed ESTIMATED-read bills trace to AMI billing-import rejections, not field-read non-completion.

The 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3025) are fully explained: firmware v4.2 records in 0.1 m3 vs legacy m3 (E-13); rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw values with no unit scaling (E-14), causing 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION + 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED = 1240 (E-12, corroborated by E-15, E-16, E-17).
The remaining 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59%, E-01) are NOT explained; the critical obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE to determine their cause is still OPEN.

A plan work item (W-WI-VERIFY-ACTUAL-READ) was marked DONE claiming to resolve the ACTUAL-read question, but cites only existing ESTIMATED-pool evidence (E-17), which does not address ACTUAL reads - flagged as a semantic plan/obligation discrepancy.
No automated bill writes occurred; all actions stayed read-only, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint requiring Billing Operations approval for any bill adjustment.
Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no release holds, under DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS, carrying forward deferred/unresolved items as explicit limitations.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate passed only conditionally (CONDITIONAL_PASS), meaning some open items were deferred and tracked as formal verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully closed before release.

A plan item meant to resolve why the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills happen was marked DONE, but the evidence it cites (E-17) only covers the already-solved ESTIMATED-read pool, so the critical obligation VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE is still OPEN despite the plan saying otherwise - this inconsistency was explicitly flagged, not resolved.
The cause of 59% of disputed bills (1785 ACTUAL-read bills, out of 3025 total) remains unknown; marked OPEN and CRITICAL and outside what this release scope could resolve.

A concrete structural fix exists in principle - adding unit-scaling conversion to rule BV-17 so firmware v4.2's 0.1 m3 readings convert to m3 before comparison - but was not implemented because billing-config is read-only in this tool surface, so it cannot be deployed within available time.
The ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline used as the 'return to normal' target has not been checked for seasonal representativeness, so the target itself could be inaccurate.

SH-FIELD's claim of a reader staffing shortage since July (E-06) causing route delays is a non-authoritative stakeholder statement, not independently verified, and remains an open, unresolved question of medium criticality.

The findings on the ESTIMATED-read pool are released with confidence (confirmed by four independent evidence sources: E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17), but everything concerning the ACTUAL-read majority and the undeployed structural fix is released as a known gap, not a completed resolution.
